summary: SDK retry boundary normalization causes multipart tool payload fragmentation and duplicate function execution
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external tool executions (webhook POSTs) originating from a single client request when using the Python and TypeScript SDKs with multipart tool payloads.

Impact:
- Zephyr Analytics (dedicated) observed duplicate downstream POSTs to their payment microservice for ~0.5% of requests during peak traffic windows starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC.
- Duplicates are side-effecting (charging) and require manual reconciliation.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: dedicated-gpu-prod-2 (us-east-1)
- SDKs: python-sdk v1.8.3 (customer pinned), ts-sdk v0.6.1
- Request pattern: streaming generation with function/tool calling; tool payloads include a multipart/related boundary and a binary attachment part (image/png) in the same request.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Start a streaming generation session that triggers a single function/tool call which includes a multipart/related body with boundary token like "----redwood-boundary-<uuid>" and a ~120KB image part.
2) Simulate transient network failure on client (close connection) causing SDK retry logic to re-establish stream and replay the outgoing tool call.
3) Observe two POSTs at downstream webhook (same payload except boundary token differs after retry).

Observed behavior / logs:
- Downstream webhooks show two POSTs within ~2s with identical form-data content but different multipart boundary strings.
- SDK client-side logs show: "retry: resending tool call (normalized headers)".
- Edge logs (us-east) show the incoming request trace ID and two proxied requests; server assigns new internal invocation IDs because boundary is treated as part of canonicalization used by the dedupe key.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should be deduplicated at the platform level for the same logical tool call (same user-supplied idempotency/nonce) even if multipart boundary tokens differ during re-serialization.

Additional notes:
- Customer uses per-request nonce header X-Redwood-Idempotency but this header is omitted by the SDK during retry normalization step for multipart requests in some code paths.
- Reproducible in both python-sdk and ts-sdk when multipart payloads include binary attachments and the SDK applies chunked re-serialization during retry.
comments: Support (Alex Chen) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged customer ticket and requested request/response traces, edge request IDs, and SDK client logs. Provided temporary workaround: set client to non-retriable for that route until we investigate (customer declined long-term).

Customer (Zephyr SRE - Jordan Miles) 2026-03-10: Uploaded sample HTTP trace (trace-id: trc-us-44822) and webhook payloads. Confirmed duplicated POSTs contain identical body bytes except multipart boundary string. Also provided SDK logs from python v1.8.3.

Support (Alex Chen) 2026-03-11: Correlated trace-id to edge session and handoff logs. Observed that dedupe key includes a canonicalized content-hash that currently includes the multipart boundary token. Raised hypothesis: SDK rewrite/normalization replaces original boundary on retry leading to different hash and new invocation. Added INT ticket to route to SDK/Runtime teams. Linked SUP-141421 -> INT-556700.

SRE (Maya Patel) 2026-03-11: Initial reproduction performed in staging. Confirmed that when SDK re-serializes multipart body it generates a new boundary token and the runtime's dedupe mechanism uses content canonicalization that includes the boundary. Creating remediation plan: runtime should ignore boundary tokens when producing canonical dedupe key for multipart/related. SDKs should preserve explicit idempotency headers across retries.

SDK Eng (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-12: Reproduced locally. Found in python-sdk v1.8.3 retry path: multipart library invocation uses uuid4() for boundary during re-serialization. Patch idea: on retry, preserve original boundary from client buffer if available; if not, runtime canonicalization must normalize boundaries prior to hashing. Preparing PRs.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- H1: SDK retry normalization drops / mutates X-Redwood-Idempotency header in multipart retry flow -> leads to new invocation. (Partial hit: header omitted sometimes.)
- H2: Runtime canonicalization includes multipart boundary in content hash -> different boundary leads to a new dedupe key. (Confirmed in staging.)
- H3: Edge proxy re-chunking splits binary attachment causing reassembly differences. (Low confidence: bytes identical except boundary.)

Findings:
- Repro reproduced with both python and ts SDKs when SDK re-serializes multipart and generates new boundary.
- Runtime dedupe key computation currently computes SHA256 over the serialized MIME body as-is (including boundary).
- Customer's X-Redwood-Idempotency header was present on initial send but SDK retry path for streaming-multipart omitted it when rebuilding the retry envelope in ~12% of attempts in a stress test.

Immediate mitigations tested:
- Runtime change: canonicalize multipart by normalizing boundary markers to a fixed token before hashing. Test in staging: dedupe key stable across retries and duplicates stop.
- SDK change: ensure idempotency header is preserved across retry envelope builds and, when re-serializing multipart, try to reuse original boundary if buffer available.
resolution:
Workaround applied (2026-03-12): Enabled runtime multipart-normalization flag in prod-us-east for the affected dedicated pool. This prevents the dedupe key from differing when only boundary tokens change. Customer confirmed duplicates dropped to 0.

Permanent fix plan:
- SDK teams: land python and ts SDK patches to preserve X-Redwood-Idempotency on retry and reuse original boundary where possible (PRs linked). Target: python-sdk v1.8.4, ts-sdk v0.6.3.
- Runtime teams: land canonicalization change to ignore boundary randomness at hash stage and add unit tests for multipart normalization. (PR referenced).
- Edge: add additional logging to detect header omission during retry envelope rebuild.

Follow-ups / action items:
- INT-556700: SDK patch and release coordination.
- INT-556701: Runtime canonicalization unit tests and rollout.
- Customer communication: draft postmortem and compensation guidance for Zephyr billing team.

Status: mitigation deployed, customer confirmed fix. Pending SDK releases and runtime merge to master.
